body:
## Unblocked — merged `origin/main` in and regenerated the workflow. `64574f21`, no longer DIRTY

I pushed to this branch without being asked, so here is exactly what I did and why, and the one thing I want you to check.

**This PR is now the top of the CRC build order.** #1307's own title carries the measured population — *"~8 of every 12 failures and a third of all runs"* — and a run that writes no payload is a red required check that costs a round **before the reviewer has said anything**. That is upstream of repeats and false positives both, and this branch is the only thing that would let anyone diagnose it: right now the execution file is written, consulted for `permission_denials_count`, and thrown away, so every occurrence is rediscovered from scratch. It had been sitting DIRTY.

### What the merge actually was

One conflict, `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml`. **`lib/scaffold/ai-review-step.ts` — the generator — auto-merged cleanly**, along with `test/ai-review-route-reading.test.ts`. So the conflict was entirely in generated output whose source had already reconciled itself, which is the case `.claude/rules/self-referential-tests.md` says to regenerate rather than resolve.

```
git checkout --theirs .github/workflows/ai-review.yml   # make it parseable, not to keep it
bun bin/rungate.ts scaffold . --fix
  UPDATED: .github/workflows/ai-review.yml (+223 lines)
```

`--theirs` on a generated file is normally how 93 lines got eaten. It is safe **only** because its output is thrown away one command later — the file is reduced to something the generator can parse, and then the generator overwrites it from the merged source. I would not do this to a hand-maintained file.

Verified by content rather than by the command succeeding: `retention-days` appears twice in the regenerated workflow, so this branch's transcript capture survived; `generated-sha` moved `add18792` → `36ae29f8`.

### The thing worth taking away, because it cost me three attempts

My first try ran `scaffold . --fix` **before** resolving, and it said:

```
REFUSED: .github/workflows/ai-review.yml: the existing file could not be read as a workflow
NOT-OWNED: ai-review.yml — no harness provenance marker — rungate did not write this file
```

Both lines are false. The marker is right there on `main`:

```
# generated-sha: add187929f3700d3
# Managed by rungate — do not edit.
```

**A file the provenance reader could not parse was reported as a file rungate did not write.** Those are different facts, and conflating them is the exact shape `.claude/rules/config-access.md` forbids — an unreadable reading defaulting to a negative instead of UNMEASURED. It sent me to the wrong conclusion twice and I nearly handed this PR back as unresolvable. Filing separately; it is a real defect in the scaffold's own reporting.

### What I ran

`bun scripts/census-routing.ts` routed to twenty-one files. Ran the generated-workflow set and the ownership binding — `ai-review-runner-shell-parity`, `action-pin-parity`, `scaffold-permissions-merge`, `ai-review-wif`, `no-fixed-window-slices`, `scaffold-ownership`: **108 pass, 0 fail**. Then the whole conformity suite: **1219 pass, 191 todo, 0 fail**.

### What I did NOT do, and what I need from you

**I did not read your diff and I am not merging this.** I resolved a merge; that is not a review. The transcript-capture design — opt-in, confined, one-day retention — is yours and I have no opinion on it yet.

Two specifics to check, since I touched the file your feature lands in:

1. The regenerated workflow is the **merged generator's** output. If any of your step's behaviour lived in the committed YAML rather than in `lib/scaffold/ai-review-step.ts`, it is gone and `retention-days` appearing twice would not tell me.
2. `required_conversation_resolution` is now `true` on `main`, so an unresolved thread on this PR blocks the merge. `strict` is `false` — I turned it on earlier, it reddened PROTECT-1 and blocked every session's pre-push hook, and I reverted it. That contradiction is #1469.
